'''Andre Jamal Drummond''' (born August 10, 1993) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player for the [[Connecticut Huskies men's basketball|University of Connecticut]]. He was one of the top rated basketball players in the class of 2012, but announced his intention to attend the University of Connecticut in the fall of 2011.

==High school career==
Andre Drummond started his high school career at Capital Preparatory Magnet School in Hartford, Connecticut. During his freshmen year he averaged 12.7 PPG, 11.9 RPG, and 6.5 BPG. (http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/cIiwRqjEhkK-vwwyncOong/basketball-winter-07-08/stats-andre-drummond.htm) He improved during his sophomore year at Capital Prep averaging 20.2 PPG, 16.6 RPG, 7.2 BLK, and 4.5 SPG. (http://www.maxpreps.com/athletes/6HpV6s2d7Emo9pJuUCdhuw/basketball-winter-08-09/stats-andre-drummond.htm). After two great years at Capital Preparatory Magnet School he transferred to St. Thomas More. At St. Thomas More in [[Oakdale, Connecticut]], Drummond was one of the most dominating [[center (basketball)|centers]] in high school basketball.<ref name=biancardi>{{cite news |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Finkelstein |first2=Adam |title=Andre Drummond to UConn surprises |date=August 26, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/6900273/still-questions-regarding-andre-drummond-commitment-connecticut |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/61FmZLGtG |archivedate=August 27, 2011}}</ref> He spent two years at St. Thomas More and led the team to the national prep championship in 2011. He graduated in the spring that year.<ref name=chardis/>

He was rated as the #1 player in the class of 2012 by ''[[ESPN]]'' and [[NBADraft.net]], while being ranked #2 player by [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Demling |first=Jody |title=Kentucky recruiting board - Class of 2012 |date=July 5, 2011 |newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]] |url=http://blogs.courier-journal.com/jodydemling/2011/07/05/kentucky-recruiting-board-class-of-2012/ |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/61FtgpfWy |archivedate=August 27, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2012mock_draft |title=2012 Mock Draft |work=NBADraft.net |publisher=Sports Phenoms, Inc |date=August 15, 2011 |archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/61FsoYyd3 |archivedate=August 27, 2011}}</ref> 

In the summer of 2010, Drummond was a member of the gold medal winning [[United States men's national basketball team|United States team]] at the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]]. He helped lead team USA to a 111-80 victory over [[Poland national basketball team|Poland]] in the gold medal game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.teamusa.org/news/2010/07/11/usa-men-s-u17-team-runs-away-with-gold-destroys-poland-111-80/37198 |title=USA Men's U17 Team Runs Away With Gold, Destroys Poland 111-80 |publisher=Basketball.TeamUSA.org |date=July 11, 2010 |accessdate=January 21, 2011}}</ref>

==NBA draft==
Drummond declared for the [[2012 NBA Draft]] on April 12, 2012.  In May 2011, ''ESPN'' wrote he has "a chance to be the No. 1 overall player in any draft he's involved with."<ref name=espnprofile>{{cite news |title=Basketball Recruiting - Andre Drummond - Player Profiles |date=May 24, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |url=http://insider.espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/evaluation?id=61194 |accessdate=August 27, 2011}}{{subscription required}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Drummond possesses NBA-like size and can rebound and block shots. In 2011, ''ESPN'' wrote that he has a developing offensive game and the ability to pass the ball in a high-low setting or with his back to the basket.<ref name=biancardi/> He can defend in the low or high post, and he is an intimidator. Drummond needs to become comfortable with his size, and avoid overaggressive play which results in foul calls.<ref name=biancardi/><ref name=espnprofile/>
